market_rationale: SPY sits at its 52-week high after a +1.2% week while breadth was mixed and the Fed is in a hiking cycle with yields rising (10y 5.24%). Cross-sectional dispersion is high (21.5%). The week contains CPI, PPI and import prices, which are the dominant catalysts; ISM prices at 74 and 3.4% PCE raise the risk of a hot print. High-beta semis, Korea and Taiwan pulled back sharply against a still-strong prior trend, which is the classic quality-pullback setup, but a hot CPI would hurt these high-beta names most. Edge is modest; I favor a selective reversal in the highest-quality pullbacks and treat the rest as no edge.
portfolio_rationale: Only the two highest-quality semiconductor-linked pullbacks, SMH and EWT, combine a top-decile prior trend, a deep recent pullback, and no in-input fundamental deterioration; they get marginal overreaction labels just above the 55% threshold. Momentum and Technology are similar but milder setups with no clear edge. Korea's drawdown and distance from highs look like trend damage, regional banks and small value show persistent weakness under a hawkish Fed, and Brazil, cybersecurity and crypto rely on price action alone. The rest of the portfolio defaults to SPY given the CPI/PPI catalyst risk.
